summary.short: Kansas SB 98 (2025) grants a sales tax exemption to qualified data center firms meeting investment, jobs and water and power commitments, bars utilities from giving data centers economic development electric discounts, and requires fusion center board review before public financial assistance to data centers.
summary.long: The act grants a sales tax exemption to qualified data centers: Kansas buildings housing networked servers, linked by fiber, and operated by a registered qualified firm. Eligibility requires commitments to invest at least $250,000,000 in eligible data center costs by the fifth year of operations, create at least 20 new jobs within two years of operations starting, buy electricity for 10 years from the certified utility, and conserve water. The exemption covers eligible costs (excluding electricity), data center equipment and related labor, lasts 20 years after commencement of operations, and is available from July 1, 2025. After a breach notice, the secretary of commerce may allow 120 days to cure, then require repayment or terminate or suspend the exemption. Section 5 bars electric utilities from applying economic development rate discounts to new or expanded data center facilities. Section 4 requires fusion center oversight board approval before public financial assistance goes to a qualified data center project, after the Kansas intelligence fusion center evaluates its equipment and software for threats to critical infrastructure.

evidence.quote: The sales tax exemption shall be valid for 20 years after the date of commencement of operations.
"Qualified data center" means one or more buildings that are constructed, reconstructed, enlarged, remodeled or leased to house a group of networked computer servers in this state
"Qualified firm" means a business or an affiliate thereof that is registered with the secretary of state and is engaged in the development, operation or leasing of a qualified data center.
"Data center equipment" means equipment or software purchased or leased for the processing, storage, retrieval or communication of data
"Eligible data center costs" means expenditures for the development, acquisition, construction and operation of a qualified data center by a qualified firm
"Commencement of operations" means the date that the qualified firm commences operations at a qualified data center
"New jobs" means newly created jobs with a qualified firm at a qualified data center or directly associated with a qualified data center
